technique.summary: Manipulate Next.js internal caching mechanisms to poison cached responses. The __nextDataReq parameter flips HTML responses to JSON format, x-now-route-matches header can trick SSG classification, and these can be combined to serve poisoned content to other users from the cache.
steps: Confirm target is running Next.js (check /_next/ paths, __NEXT_DATA__ in source, x-nextjs-* headers)
Test __nextDataReq=1 parameter: append to any SSR page URL — if response flips from HTML to JSON, the parameter is processed
Check cache headers (x-nextjs-cache, x-vercel-cache, cache-control) to confirm caching behavior
Test x-now-route-matches header: send header with route parameters to trick SSG classification
Combine __nextDataReq with cache poisoning: if JSON response gets cached, all users receive broken JSON instead of HTML
Test x-matched-path header as alternative to x-now-route-matches
Verify poison persists by requesting the same URL without the poison parameter

payloads.notes: Flips SSR HTML response to JSON data format — if cached, serves JSON to all users expecting HTML
Header that tricks Next.js SSG route classification — may serve different page content
Alternative header for route matching manipulation on Vercel-hosted Next.js
Direct Next.js data route — may bypass cache key isolation and serve page data

bypassTechniques: URL-encode __nextDataReq: __%6eextDataReq=1 or %5f%5fnextDataReq=1 to bypass WAF rules
Try x-matched-path header if x-now-route-matches is blocked
Target locale-prefixed routes: /en/page?__nextDataReq=1 — locale routing may have different cache behavior
Direct /_next/data/ paths: access data routes directly to bypass page-level cache protections
Combine with Accept-Encoding variations: different encodings may create separate cache entries to poison
Test on preview/staging deployments which may have weaker cache protections
